The issue requires preserving leading slashes in S3 presigned URLs when they start with `//`. This was identified in `src/requests/adapters.py` within the `request_url` method.

The problematic logic that collapsed leading slashes was:
```python
        url = request.path_url
        if url.startswith("//"):  # Don't confuse urllib3
            url = f"/{url.lstrip('/')}"
```
I have replaced this logic with a minimal change that removes the specific slash collapsing behavior, while keeping the surrounding logic intact.

The fix has been applied to `src/requests/adapters.py`.

I will now submit the patch.
